title: Possessive Adjectives: My, Your, His, Her, Its, Our, Their
summary: Learn how to show who owns something using words like my, your, and his. These words make your English sound natural and clear.

sections.p: Possessive adjectives show who owns a thing. We put these words right before a noun. For example, we say 'my pen' or 'your bag'. They change depending on who has the thing. We use 'my' for I, 'your' for you, 'his' for a man, and 'her' for a woman.

sections.h: Talking about Animals, Groups, and Everyone
sections.p: We use 'its' for animals or things, like a dog or a phone. We use 'our' when something belongs to you and me together. We use 'their' when something belongs to a group of other people. Always match the word to the owner, not the object.

ex.mean: The tail belongs to the dog.

words.mean: belongs to an animal or thing

tip: Look at the person who owns the thing to choose the right word. Remember: He = his, She = her, They = their!

quiz.en: I have a cat. ___ name is Luna.
You are a student. Where is ___ backpack?
John is here. This is ___ jacket.
We live in this city. ___ street is quiet.
The children are playing with ___ toys.
